newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary, Romania sign pact against organised crime.
newsitem.headline: Hungary, Romania sign pact against organised crime.

text.p: Hungary and Romania, in a further move to consolidate closer relations, signed an accord on Wednesday to tackle organised crime, drug trafficking and terrorism.

"We have common problems as both countries regard themselves as a transit territory (for organised crime)," Hungarian Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze told a news conference after signing the agreement with his Romanian counterpart, Gavril Dejeu.

Dejeu said that the agreement calls for closer cooperation between the police forces and border guards of the two countries and added his ministry was drafting new laws that would improve the legal framework for law enforcement.
"Our ministry plans to put some 12 to 13 new laws before parliament dealing with all areas of crime," Dejeu said.
In answer to a question Kuncze said Romanian citizens accounted for 40 percent of all crime committed by foreigners in Hungary.
Dejeu, on only his second foreign visit since taking office, said the new Romanian government was keen on improving relations with neighbouring countries.

Such a policy has been praised in recent weeks by leading Western politicians such as British Foreign Minister Malcolm Rifkind and French President Jacques Chirac, who have indicated Romania's chances of early integration into NATO and the European Union are improving as a result.
On Monday the Romanian and Hungarian defence ministers signed an accord on the protection of military secrets and agreed to set up a joint peacekeeping battalion.
Romanian Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea is expected to further consolidate bilateral links when he visits Hungary in mid-March.
